subject: Evaluation kickoff: proposed slots, trial plan & success metrics
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Morales <elena@wellpath.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-07T20:15:00-08:00
Subject: Evaluation kickoff: proposed slots, trial plan & success metrics

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for a productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap so we’re aligned before scheduling the kickoff:

- Key goals you called out: reduce triage time for clinical notes, increase extraction accuracy for med/diagnosis entities, and measure impact on downstream chart review throughput.
- Scope: 2-week evaluation against a 2k-sample prompt set (de-identified) focusing on inpatient discharge notes and ambulatory visit summaries.
- Primary constraints: PHI handling (anonymization), no external data moves, and SSO required for Redwood console.

Next step: schedule the evaluation kickoff (trial plan + tech deep dive). Proposed slots (PT):
- Wed Nov 11, 10:00–11:00 AM PT — preferred (includes an ops + eng break-out)
- Thu Nov 12, 9:00–10:00 AM PT — fallback

I’ve attached a draft trial plan and a prompt set template to this thread (trial_plan_v1.pdf, prompt_set_template.csv). The kickoff will cover success criteria, test data approach, shipping prompts, and security prework.

Can you confirm which slot works, and who from your engineering/security team I should invite? If you prefer, I can send a calendar invite for the Nov 11 slot and include an agenda.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: trial_plan_v1.pdf, prompt_set_template.csv

Cc: Procurement <procurement@wellpath.health>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff: proposed slots, trial plan & success metrics

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear recap.

We’d like to go with the Nov 11 slot (10–11 AM PT). Please include a short agenda that separates the product demo from the technical breakout.

A couple of questions before kickoff:
1) For success criteria, our team will want both precision/recall on entity extraction and an operational metric (reduction in manual chart review time). Do you have a recommended threshold you usually aim for in pilots?
2) Can Redwood support anonymization on our side (we can run a de-ident pipeline) or do you need us to provide de-identified samples only?

I’m looping in procurement and will add our engineering lead on reply — please CC Diego (diego_fernandez@wellpath.health) on the invite.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Clinical Data & Analytics
WellPath Health

Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff: proposed slots, trial plan & success metrics

Perfect — I’ll lock Nov 11 for 10–11 AM PT and send an invite with the agenda. Agenda preview:
- 10:00–10:15 AM: Goals & success metrics (Naomi)
- 10:15–10:35 AM: Product walkthrough + demo prompts (Ben)
- 10:35–10:55 AM: Technical deep dive & data/security Qs (Marissa + Diego)
- 10:55–11:00 AM: Next steps & owners

Suggested success metrics (to start the pilot conversation):
- Entity extraction: precision >= 88% and recall >= 80% on target entity set (medications, diagnoses, procedures)
- Operational: 30% reduction in average manual review time per chart within the 2-week window
- Stability: <1% error rate on inference calls during business hours

On anonymization: we support either approach. If you run a de-id pipeline and provide de-identified samples, that is fine (recommended for fastest start). If you prefer Redwood to perform edge anonymization, we can run an internal pipeline (must be scoped in the trial plan and will require a short security addendum).

I’ve updated the trial plan with those success metrics and attached the spreadsheet (trial_plan_v1_updated.xlsx) and included a shared doc link. Please confirm Diego as the engineering contact and let us know if procurement needs anything else ahead of the kickoff.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
